Mr. Frederick Pitts
Police Headquarters

Dear Sir,
We are herewith applying for entry permits for approximately
25 Rabbis with families and approximately 75 students of
Jewish theological seminaries. They are Polish citizens now
refugees in Lithuania. All of them have special recommendations
for visas from State Department of Washington D. C., and will
proceed to United States from here. From time to time Rabbi
Ashkenazi will submit the names of individuals for whom these
permits will be required.

We have consulted with Dr. Newman who came from United States
as representative of Union of Orthodox Rabbis of U. S. and
Canada, and other religious organizations, and who has made
arrangements to cover transportation and all other costs.

We guarantee to provide for all the needs of these people, and
to assure that they do not become public charges.
Your efforts in their behalf will be greatly appreciated.

Respectfully yours,
Rabbi M. Ashkenazy President
H. Drucker
Treasurer

File No. 6422 (I)
Special Branch - S.W. Station, 3rd
REPORT
Date March 6, 1941
Subject Central European Refugee Affairs - Immigration into Shanghai
from Soviet-occupied Poland of rabbis, theologists, etc.
Made by D.S.I. Pitts Forwarded by C.D.I. Tabrum 20/3/41
A.I.

During the afternoon of March 5, 1941 Mr. E.
KANN of the Committee for the Assistance to European
Jewish Refugees in Shanghai introduced to me Mr.
Frank NEWMAN whom, he stated, had arrived in Shanghai
from America on a special mission connected with
the emigration of Jewish rabbis, theologists, learned-
men, etc. from Soviet-occupied areas in Europe.
Mr. NEWMAN has produced proper credentials showing
that he is an accredited representative of
(1) Emergency Committee for War Torn Yeshivoth,
673 Broadway, New York City,
(2) Agudath Israel Youth Council of America,
616 Bedford Avenue, Brooklyn, N.Y.
(3) The Union of Orthodox Rabbis of the
United States and Canada,
673 Broadway, New York City.

He has been in Japan for a number of weeks
making arrangements with the American Consular and
Japanese Foreign Office officials in matters
connected with the transfer of many well-known Jewish
rabbis and theological students from the European
War zone and adjacent territories to the United
States via Japan. Most of these individuals are
from the former territories of Lithuania and Poland
now occupied by Soviet Russia.
These rabbis and students spend their entire lives
in studying Jewish theological questions and from
these men are selected those members who are destined to
carry on the tenets of the Jewish faith throughout
the world.

事由 中欧难民事务 - 来自苏占波兰的拉比、神学家等人员移居上海事宜
制作人 D.S.I. 皮茨 转呈人 C.D.I. 塔布鲁姆 1941年3月20日
A.I.

1941年3月5日下午，上海欧洲犹太难民援助委员会的 E.
坎恩先生向我介绍了弗兰克·纽曼先生，据称，纽曼先生
从美国抵达上海，执行一项与犹太拉比、神学家、学者
等从欧洲苏占地区移民有关的特殊任务。
纽曼先生出示了适当的证明文件，表明他是以下机构的认证代表：
(1) 战火中的叶史瓦紧急委员会，
纽约市百老汇大道 673 号，
(2) 美国以色列青年理事会，
纽约州布鲁克林贝德福德大道 616 号，
(3) 美国和加拿大正统拉比联盟，
纽约市百老汇大道 673 号。

他在日本停留了数周，
与美国领事馆官员和日本外务省官员就
将许多著名的犹太拉比和神学学生从欧洲
战区及周边领土经日本转移至美国的事宜
做出安排。这些人大多来自
前立陶宛和波兰领土，现已被苏联俄罗斯占领。
这些拉比和学生终其一生都在研究犹太神学问题，
并从这些人中选出注定要在
全世界传承犹太教义信条的成员。

（左侧批注及印章）

结论中同意
他们受到限制
在此之后
